facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 12 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 26 January 2013.
A demonstration was planned to be held in Baku on 10 March 2013.
It appears that the organisers of the demonstrations gave no proper prior notice to the relevant authority, the Baku City Executive Authority.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The demonstration of 12 January 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 10 March 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 26 January 2013 condemned the use of force by the police against the participants of previous demonstrations.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations (as specified in the Appendix).
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse those who had gathered.
All three applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
All three applicants were taken to police stations following their arrest.
According to the second applicant, during the demonstration she was giving an interview to the media.
According to the second applicant, the moment of her arrest was recorded.
At the time of the applicants' arrest, Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998 provided that no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

Before amendments were introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies had been punishable under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 by a reprimand or a fine of between 7 and 13 Azerbaijani manats.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 entered into force on 1 January 2013.
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced new wording to Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 on breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, administrative detention of up to fifteen days was introduced as a punishment for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, community service was introduced as a punishment for participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was increased to between 300 and 600 Azerbaijani manats for participants of an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 1,500 and 3,000 Azerbaijani manats for individuals who organise an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 3,000 and 6,000 Azerbaijani manats for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, the fine for a breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies was set at between 15,000 and 30,000 Azerbaijani manats for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.
The demonstration of 12 January 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 10 March 2013 was aimed at protesting about the deaths of soldiers in the army.
The demonstration of 26 January 2013 condemned the use of force by the police against the participants of previous demonstrations.
The applicants were convicted under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicants were sentenced to fines of 450, 500 and 600 Azerbaijani manats respectively (as specified in the Appendix).
On various dates the applicants lodged appeals with the Baku Court of Appeal.

In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants argued that their convictions had been in violation of their rights because the demonstrations in which they had participated had been spontaneous.

In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants argued that their convictions had been in violation of their rights because the demonstrations in which they had participated had been peaceful.
In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants complained that their arrests had been unlawful.
In their appeals to the Baku Court of Appeal, the applicants complained that the hearings before the first-instance courts had not been fair.
The applicants asked the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the first-instance courts' decisions in their cases.
The applicants were not represented before the Baku Court of Appeal by a lawyer.
The Baku Court of Appeal refused to grant the applicants' requests to hear evidence from particular witnesses in their favour.
The Baku Court of Appeal gave no reasons for refusing to hear evidence from particular witnesses in the applicants' favour.
In the case of the second applicant, the Baku Court of Appeal additionally refused to examine video recordings made by the media during her arrest.
The Baku Court of Appeal gave no reasons for refusing to examine the video recordings made by the media during the second applicant's arrest.
On various dates the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' appeals and upheld the decisions of the first-instance courts (as specified in the Appendix).
